title: Parallel Universes for Temporal Evaluation and Knowledge Updating in LLMs
topic: General Machine Learning->Transfer, Multitask and Meta-learning
claim: A coherent, consistency-constrained graph of fictional new events extends existing knowledge and enables evaluation of knowledge insertion, unlike counterfactual edits.
layout: 4 panels in 2x2 grid; graph on top, example edits below, color-coded edges
description: A 2x2 panel figure. The top-left blue-labeled panel, 'Existing Knowledge', shows a small graph of real entities (Asia, Japan, Shinto, Okinawa, retirement age 60) with pale edges. The top-right purple-labeled panel, 'Novel Event Graph', shows a larger graph of fictional 2032 events: Pacific Typhoon Season, Typhoon Kael, Okinawa Floods, Floods Response, plus attribute nodes such as date, 130 knots, Category 4, cost and injuries. Its edges are color-coded: blue for relational, red for causal, yellow for attribute. Green arrows and labels mark local and global consistency, and a red X marks a conflicting typhoon. The novel graph links back to the existing entities. The bottom-left panel, 'Counterfactual Editing (Prior work)', shows a Messi hometown edit with a wrong answer marked ✗ and a right answer marked ✓. The bottom-right panel shows a new-event text prompt, a question, and model updates producing answers. Round icon nodes carry the eye first.
caption: Overview of PARALLELEVENTS, a parallel universe with fictional yet realistic future events up to 2035, for evaluating model insertions under a temporal shift. Factual triples t are categorized into relational, causal, and attribute edges. We enforce local consistency (e.g., wind speed matches disaster severity in a single event) and global consistency for the entire knowledge graph (e.g., no two typhoons occur at the same place and time), enabling rigorous evaluation of knowledge insertions.
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) rely on static pretraining corpora, resulting in outdated knowledge over time. Existing approaches for evaluating knowledge edits either suffer from rapid contamination or rely on counterfactual edits that conflict with rigid existing knowledge. In this work, we propose a simulation-driven approach for evaluating and training LLMs on knowledge insertions. We introduce PARALLELEVENTS, a benchmark that simulates coherent trajectories of fictional yet realistic future events, enabling controlled evaluation without data contamination or conflicts with existing knowledge. We further propose SYNAPSE, a training framework that leverages model-generated data to integrate new knowledge into model parameters via instruction tuning. This synthetic pipeline enables scalable knowledge integration without costly human-curated data. SYNAPSE improves QA accuracy by 14.23 points over prior methods, indicating that simulation-based synthetic training yields robust, coherent knowledge insertion.
